name: Daund–Koraput Highway
aka: Nizamabad–Jagdalpur section was the former NH 16 (old numbering)
history: NH 63 is one of the long east–west roads of central India. From Daund, a railway town in Pune district, it crosses the Marathwada plain through Barshi, Latur and Udgir, runs across northern Telangana through Nizamabad, Jagtial and Mancherial, and then winds through the forests of Bastar in Chhattisgarh before ending at Koraput in the hills of Odisha. Much of its middle portion carried the number NH 16 before the highways were renumbered.
facts: About 1,065 km long, crossing Maharashtra, Telangana, Chhattisgarh and Odisha.
Crosses three big rivers on its way: the Godavari, the Pranahita and the Indravati.
Passes through Jagdalpur, the main town of the forested Bastar region.
Its Nizamabad–Jagdalpur portion was the old NH 16.
